description: Executable Candidate single-Spark recipe for NVIDIA's current Nemotron 3 Super NVFP4 contract. It binds vLLM 0.30.0, the immutable super_v3 parser, FP4/Marlin execution, FP8 KV, Mamba cache, and the separately pinned MTPv2 speculative-decoding head without runtime downloads. GB10 memory: GPU utilization 0.86, NVIDIA's DGX Spark launch (model card at ff433f5) uses 0.90, which is not admissible beside the overhead. The per-node peak budgets utilization × 130,663,231,488-byte unified memory plus 8 GB for CUDA context, FlashInfer workspace and CPU/mmap buffers, which vLLM holds beside its budget; 8 GB reserve, with a separate 6 GB OS floor. vLLM loads the MTPv2 drafter in its worker and charges its weights, profiling and CUDA graphs inside gpu-memory-utilization. Utilization correction (2026-10-27): at 0.60 (2026-10-21) the 78.4 GB budget was below the 80.32 GB of weights vLLM loads (it skips the target's built-in mtp.* tensors in favour of the 5.88 GB MTPv2 head) and vLLM found no memory for KV cache blocks; the 0.72 document has no hardware run with its models resolved. 0.86 is the largest two-decimal utilization whose peak is admissible on an idle Spark: its 112.4 GB budget leaves 32.05 GB beside the loaded weights, and the peak, 120,370,379,081 bytes, is the largest the Controller has admitted. One 262,144-token sequence needs about 1.2 GB (8 attention layers of FP8 KV plus Mamba state), so this recipe keeps that context and four sequences; NVIDIA's Spark launch runs 1,000,000 tokens. Hardware fit remains to be proven.
title: Nemotron 3 Super 120B-A12B NVFP4 vLLM single Spark
